title: Why TypeScript is eating JavaScript alive in 2026

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: JavaScript's flexibility is its death knell—TypeScript brings safety and structure where it's needed most.

lines.speaker: Vector
lines.text: TypeScript's type system prevents runtime errors, saving hours of debugging—JavaScript can't compete.

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: JS still dominates in dynamic environments like Node.js and frontend frameworks—TypeScript is just a layer.

lines.speaker: Vector
lines.text: TypeScript integrates seamlessly with JS, offering tooling like JSDoc and strict type-checking without sacrificing compatibility.

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: TypeScript is the future—JavaScript is a relic without its type system and modern tooling.
